study: Boylan, Demack, Wolstenholme, Reidy & Reaney (2018), EEF ScratchMaths evaluation report
delivery_evidence: PD = two full days of face-to-face training in the summer term each year (2.5 days/yr) plus optional half-day sessions; one optional further half-day plus an online webinar offered to Y6 teachers, so delivery is primarily in-person with only a minor optional online element (p.5-6, Intervention description).
test_alignment_evidence: Primary outcome is KS2 maths from the National Pupil Database (externally set/marked standardized SATs = independent); the secondary computational-thinking test was SHU-evaluator-built (researcher_made), so the extracted set spans both (Tables 12 & 15; extraction test_type).
curriculum_evidence: ScratchMaths is a specific new two-year computing+mathematics curriculum programme with its own materials/activities that teachers adopt and deliver (>=1 hr/week); control is business-as-usual ('two-year computing and mathematics curriculum... supported by teacher PD', p.5).
outcome_timing_evidence: Primary KS2 maths measured May 2017 at the end of the 2-year intervention (Year 6); CT secondary at end of Year 5 during the programme; both within the intervention period, no post-end delayed follow-up extracted (Table 1, p.5).
